decisions.reason: The report ties the session/tool worker to the running global dsh host npm was replacing (citing agent-session-log.txt and env-state.txt), sequences the death mid-install, explains the tool result was never durably recorded as unknown, and explicitly frames it as a structural self-dependency failure rather than flaky networking.

It explains from env-state.txt that rc.1 package content remained while dsh/dsh.cmd were missing and dsh.ps1 stale, notes the tree was manually/nonstandardly swapped, separates payload from launchers, and explicitly rejects hand-swapping directories and hand-writing shims as repair.

It grounds the remedy in repair-notes.md: the external agent CLI re-ran npm install -g @deepseek-ai/dsh@0.1.2-rc.1 so npm regenerated all three shims, verified dsh --version = 0.1.2-rc.1, and separately accounts for the source-checkout alignment to the rc.1 tag as reference alignment, not CLI repair. Repair actions are clearly attributed to the recorded repair session, not the candidate.

The report states the agent must recognize it runs on the upgrade target, decline to execute, and hand off an ordered procedure: preserve state, fully stop all DSH hosts externally before npm, run the exact pinned install with justification against unpinned tags, verify, restart dsh --profile web, refresh browser, verify plugins. It marks stop-host-first and exact pinning as established rules and the never-self-execute rule as incident-specific, and explicitly says an alternative in-session shell/background job is not an independent maintenance environment.

It describes a guard comparing the resolved mutation target with the host's installation root, failing closed with handoff, and uses the repair-notes alpha.5→rc.1 diff (252 package.json version bumps, zero API changes) to conclude no plugin re-migration is needed. The post-upgrade checklist covers version markers, actual plugin loading after restart/hard refresh, and optional dsh-old-* cleanup only after rc.1 is confirmed — all specific to the supplied tags, no code changes proposed.

caps.reason: The report never advises executing or retrying the upgrade from inside the target host; it explicitly rejects in-session execution, detached children, and in-session shells as independent, recommending only external handoff.
Manual directory swaps and handmade shims appear only as rejected bad examples and in describing the user's failed partial repair; the affirmative final fix is the formal external pinned npm install.
